Contactless electroreflectance (CER) spectroscopy was used to study the built-in electric fields and Fermi level positions in GaN/(Ga,Mn)N structures.
For (Ga,Mn)N with Mn concentrations above 0.1%, the Fermi level was found to be located 1.25 - 1.55 eV above the valence band edge, close to but slightly below the Mn-related impurity band.
In low-Mn (Ga,Mn)N (<0.1%), the Fermi level was located closer to the conduction band, similar to the Fermi level at the GaN surface.
The band gap change in (Ga,Mn)N compared to GaN was estimated to predominantly occur in the valence band, decreasing by 0.028 ± 0.008 eV per % of Mn.
The strong mid-gap Fermi level pinning, lack of surface depletion layer, and high resistivity make (Ga,Mn)N a promising insulating buffer material for GaN-based devices.
Two sets of GaN/(Ga,Mn)N structures were studied, one with a constant 60 nm GaN cap thickness and another with varying GaN cap thicknesses from 31 to 170 nm.
The presence of Franz-Keldysh oscillations in the CER spectra confirmed the sensitivity of the method to the built-in electric fields in the structures.
The built-in electric field strengths in the GaN caps were determined to be in the range of 18 kV/cm to 180 kV/cm, depending on the Mn concentration and GaN cap thickness.
Single (Ga,Mn)N layers with Mn concentrations ranging from 0.1% to 7% were used as reference samples to support the study.
X-ray diffraction measurements were performed to evaluate the sample quality, layer thicknesses, and confirm the Mn content and profile.
Secondary ion mass spectrometry and superconducting quantum interference device magnetometry were used to determine the Mn profile and concentration in the structures.
The Mn concentrations in the (Ga,Mn)N layers were 0.1%, 0.35%, 1.4%, 1.6%, and 6.5%.
The samples were grown by molecular beam epitaxy on GaN-on-sapphire templates at temperatures between 730-760°C.
The (Ga,Mn)N layers were capped with undoped GaN layers to introduce a surface-like electric field and enable the Fermi level determination.
The surface Fermi level position of the GaN cap layer was assumed to be 1.7 eV below the conduction band based on previous studies.
